items.title: Clem Raymond Interview, 1958-08-25
items.q: You say George Barquet got yours fest for you?

ctx.x: It was improved for the ones I had. It didn't have no keys or no rolls or nothing. But I always used a buffet because that's what Papa Teal had. The clarinet players there, if you didn't have a buffet, you didn't have no clarinet.

What kind of fest has gotten? You say George Barquet got yours fest for you? Yeah, Malcolm, Alfred Wilson. Oh, yeah, piano player. I'm always going to ask what kind of a reed you use. Do you use a stiff reed or medium or soft? What kind of a reed do you like?

Well, since I don't play so often, I use a number three. They call that almost medium. Yeah, number three. And then when I play band music, I have what they call a plastic reed. It's a number four. It don't become water soap. It changes the tone. You don't get a sweeter tone or a soft tone like you would. So playing street music, you want to hear the clarinet. And most of the clarinet players around here, they're used to sitting down and play, and they can't walk in place. So I try to help out. But I play strong.…
